$comment: D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE (TF-C62): GNU `__attribute__((...))` in the AFTER-DECLARATOR position with the widened argument grammar — `format(printf,1,2)` (multi-arg), `__nothrow__,__leaf__` (multi-clause), `__nonnull__((1))` (nested paren), `alloc_size(1)` (number). This is the shape every real C header uses on its prototypes (glibc `__attribute__((__nothrow__,__leaf__))`, Tcl `TCL_FORMAT_PRINTF(1,2)`). The attributes are parse-and-ignore hints — the program must COMPILE and RUN with them present: add(v,12)+deref(&10)+logfmt("%d",7)+raw-is-non-null = 32+10+0+0 = 42. RED-ON-DISABLE: revert the after-declarator attrSpec slot in initDeclarator -> the first prototype fails P0009 -> the program no longer compiles (compile failure, not exit 42). The release arm re-witnesses the attributed declarations survive the shipped pipeline. ★ TF-C73 reworked the attribute set: (a) `aligned(4)` LEFT — the trailing position is now scanned like the leading one, and accepting it here meant silently dropping the alignment. That departure was pinned 'it comes back when the real `aligned` sink lands, asserting the ALIGNMENT, not merely the parse'; the sink LANDED in TF-C73 and the case came back in `examples/c/gnu_aligned_attribute/`, NOT here, because that example gates its exit code on the RUNTIME ADDRESS of an over-aligned global in each position — strictly stronger than restoring a row that could only re-prove the declaration compiles (and `aligned(4)` on an `int` is not even an over-alignment, so it could never have failed). This file owns the ARGUMENT GRAMMAR on parse-and-ignore hints; alignment HONORING is the other example's job; (b) the `format` witness was INVALID C that clang REJECTS (`format argument not a string type` — it sat on `int firstv(int n, ...)`) and now sits on a genuine `const char *fmt` format function; (c) the number-arg role moved to `alloc_size(1)` on a POINTER-returning allocator, where that attribute legally applies. The whole file is VERIFIED clang-clean (`-Wall -Wextra`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang-built binary also exits 42 — a corpus example must witness REAL C, not merely C that DSS happens to accept.
